details: CONFIRMED by repro (below) for "global"; "settings" and "agents" by reading relay_rules.sync lines 291 and 308-312: the special
targets are selected by membership of their names in `only`. register_project returns False for an existing name, so the
"global" project is never registered with its own file; the sync then renders and adopts the global target.
The line was changed in this branch precisely to keep global targets out (it dropped "global" from only), so the fix belongs here.
Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH: it breaks decision A only for these three names, and a .before-relay copy is kept.
evidence: S=<scratchpad>/repro; git init -q $S/global; echo "my own file" > $S/claude/CLAUDE.md
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$S/claude RELAY_HOME=$S/home RELAY_PROJECTS=$S/projects.toml RELAY_SKIP_PAID_DUE=1 python3 bin/relay setup $S/global
<!-- Generated by relay (relay sync). Edit rules/ and profiles/active.toml, not this file. -->
failing_case: Temporary HOME (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<tmp>/claude holding CLAUDE.md "my own file"), projects.toml with the usual [global] target,
RELAY_SKIP_PAID_DUE=1; `git init <tmp>/global`; `bin/relay setup <tmp>/global`.
Now: exit 0, "Synced: global written", <tmp>/claude/CLAUDE.md is relay's generated file and CLAUDE.md.before-relay appears.
cmd_setup calls relay_rules.sync(only={d["name"]}, adopt=d["name"]) and the project name "global" is the global target's
name, so it is synced and adopted. A folder named "settings" hits `if not only or "settings" in only` and rewrites
~/.claude/settings.json (model, effort, env); "agents" rewrites the installed agents.
Should: the Claude folder byte-identical, as for any other project (owner's decision A: project setup never writes the user's files).
fix_hint: In cmd_setup (or relay_setup.setup/register_project), refuse a project name that is a reserved sync target ("global",
"settings", "agents", or any target whose file is under claude_dir()) with a message asking for another folder name; or call a
sync of exactly the project's registered target that skips the special names. Add the "global" repro as a test in a temp HOME.
pass_cases: 1. Folder named "global", temp HOME with CLAUDE.md "my own file": `relay setup <dir>` leaves every file under the Claude folder
byte-identical (no CLAUDE.md.before-relay); setup either refuses the name with a message or syncs only the project's own target.
2. Folder named "settings": `relay setup <dir>` leaves ~/.claude/settings.json absent/byte-identical.
3. Folder named "agents": no agent file outside the project changes.
4. Folder named "proj" (today's case): setup writes the project's CLAUDE.local.md and exit 0 as now.
reason: tests/test_setup_off.py:369 (folder named global leaves Claude folder alone) and :379 (ordinary name still sets up); the first fails at 4cab4b6.
findings.summary: a project whose folder is named global, settings or agents makes `relay setup <dir>` write the user's global files

details: CONFIRMED by reading the order of flag() calls in cmd_setup. Low: nothing wrong is written, a flag is lost.
evidence: bin/relay:397-405: apply/flow/specs/product consumed, then `if flag(args, "--global", ...)`: `if migrate or any(a != "--no-claude" for a in args)`
failing_case: `relay setup --global --specs openspec`: --flow/--specs/--product/--no-product/--apply are taken out of args before the
--global test (bin/relay:397-401), so `any(a != "--no-claude" for a in args)` sees nothing and install() runs; exit 0, the
spec flag is ignored. The usage message the code holds for this case ("--global takes nothing else") is never shown.
Should: exit 2 with "--global takes nothing else: relay setup --global [--no-claude]".
fix_hint: Test for "--global" first (before the other flag() calls) and refuse when any other argument is present.
pass_cases: 1. `relay setup --global --specs openspec` -> exit 2, the --global usage message, nothing written.
2. `relay setup --global --flow issues` -> exit 2.
3. `relay setup --global` and `relay setup --global --no-claude` -> run install as now.
4. `relay setup <dir> --global` -> exit 2 as now.
reason: tests/test_setup_off.py:385 --global with a project flag is a usage error; fails at 4cab4b6.
findings.summary: `relay setup --global --flow issues` (or --specs, --product, --apply) runs the global install and drops the project flags silently
